# Appendix A: Data Generation for Simulation Studies

Data were generated in three stages: (i) exogenous latent predictors, (ii) dependent latent variables through the structural model, and (iii) observed indicators through the measurement model.

**Exogenous Predictors.** Predictor latent variables were specified to follow covariance structures
\[
\boldsymbol{\Phi}_1 = 
\begin{bmatrix} 
1 & 0.375 \\ 
0.375 & 1 
\end{bmatrix}
\quad \text{(Simulation 1)}, \qquad
\boldsymbol{\Phi}_2 = 
\begin{bmatrix} 
1 & 0.3 & 0.2 \\ 
0.3 & 1 & 0.3 \\ 
0.2 & 0.3 & 1 
\end{bmatrix}
\quad \text{(Simulation 2)}.
\]

Data were generated using the VITA as implemented in the *covsim* package (version `r covsim_version`) [@R-covsim] with sampling via *rvinecopulib* (version `r vinecop`) [@R-rvinecopulib]. Under the normal condition, predictors had Gaussian marginals with the specified covariance structure. Under the right-skewed condition, gamma marginals with shape $=1$ and rate $=1$ were employed, producing skewness $\gamma_1 = 2$ and excess kurtosis $\gamma_2 = 6$. Under the uniform condition, predictors were generated from $U[-\sqrt{3\phi_{kk}}, \sqrt{3\phi_{kk}}]$, ensuring that each marginal variance matched the target value ($\phi_{kk}$ is the diagonal element of $\boldsymbol{\Phi}$). In all distributional conditions, VITA constructed a vine copula to impose the specified dependence structure while preserving the marginal distributions.

**Structural Model.** Dependent latent variables were generated according to the structural equations, with residual variances $\psi$ calibrated to yield
\[
R^2_\eta = \frac{\operatorname{Var}(\eta^*)}{\operatorname{Var}(\eta^*) + \psi} \approx 0.30,
\]

where $\eta^*$ denotes the deterministic portion of the dependent latent variable. Structural residuals were sampled from $\mathcal{N}(0,\psi)$.

**Measurement Model.** Indicators were generated as
\[
\mathbf{y} = \boldsymbol{\Lambda}\boldsymbol{\eta} + \boldsymbol{\epsilon}, \quad 
\boldsymbol{\epsilon} \sim \mathcal{N}(\mathbf{0}, \boldsymbol{\Theta}),
\]

with unit factor loadings ($\lambda_j = 1$) and error variances $\theta_{jj}$ set to achieve reliabilities
\[
\rho_{y_j} = \frac{\lambda_j^2 \phi_{kk}}{\lambda_j^2 \phi_{kk} + \theta_{jj}} \approx \rho, \quad \rho \in \{0.4, 0.6, 0.8\}.
\]

Each latent variable was measured by three indicators.

**Fixed Variance Parameters.** Population models were first "calibrated" under normally distributed predictors to achieve the desired reliabilities ($\rho \approx 0.4,0.6,0.8$) and $R^2 \approx 0.30$. The resulting structural residual variances ($\psi$) and measurement error variances ($\theta_{jj}$) were then held fixed across all distributional conditions, ensuring that differences in estimation performance were attributable solely to violations of distributional assumptions.
